tasks.gr8-biogeochemical-cycles-t2: Topic: Biogeochemical cycles. Cover water, carbon, and nitrogen cycles, decomposers, atmosphere interactions, and matter recycling through living and non-living systems. Ask Grade 8 learners to trace cycle stages, interpret cycle diagrams, and explain cause-and-effect links in cycling matter.
tasks.gr8-solar-system-and-gravity-t2: Topic: Solar system and gravity. Cover the Sun, planets, moons, comets, asteroids, relative scale ideas, and gravity as the force keeping objects in orbit. Ask Grade 8 learners to order objects, compare planetary properties, and explain gravitational effects in familiar space contexts.
tasks.gr8-particle-model-and-states-t2: Topic: The particle model of matter. Cover the particle model as a scientific theory (particles too small to see, the spaces between them are empty), the arrangement, movement, forces and spacing of particles in a solid, liquid and gas, change of state (melting, evaporating or boiling, condensing, freezing) explained by particle movement, and diffusion from high to low concentration (faster in gases than in liquids). Ask Grade 8 learners to describe states with the particle model and to explain changes of state and diffusion.
tasks.gr8-density-expansion-pressure-t2: Topic: Density, expansion and contraction, and gas pressure. Cover density as the mass in a given volume (equal volumes of different materials have different masses), floating of less dense materials (oil on water, ice on water), expansion when heated and contraction when cooled explained by the spaces between particles (size and number of particles do not change), and gas pressure from particle collisions (more particles, more collisions). Do not use density formulae or the effect of temperature on pressure (Grade 9). Ask Grade 8 learners to compare, predict and explain.
tasks.gr8-atoms-elements-compounds-t2: Topic: Atoms, elements, compounds and mixtures. Cover atoms as the building blocks of matter, elements (the first 20 on the Periodic Table), the sub-atomic particles (protons positive and neutrons neutral in the nucleus, electrons negative around it), neutral atoms, molecules of elements (H₂, N₂, O₂, Cl₂), compounds with fixed ratios (H₂O, CO₂, NaCl), chemical bonds, decomposition by heating or electrolysis, and mixtures separated by physical means. Ask Grade 8 learners to describe atoms, classify substances and explain the difference between elements, compounds and mixtures.
tasks.gr8-reactants-and-products-t2: Topic: Chemical reactions: reactants and products. Cover reactants and products in word and symbol equations (C + O₂ → CO₂, 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O), rearrangement of atoms with the bonds of the reactants breaking and new bonds forming, the egg in white vinegar and the limewater test as examples, and fermentation in brewing as indigenous knowledge. Balancing equations is Grade 9. Ask Grade 8 learners to identify reactants and products and to explain the evidence of a reaction.
